name: Danish

ancestors.notes: Descent from Old Norse (East Norse branch)
Low German / Hanseatic adstrate: even stronger than Swedish due to geographic proximity and political union

notes: Standard Danish (rigsdansk). QUANTITY: a stressed vowel is long in an open syllable / before a single consonant and short before a consonant cluster or a doubled consonant letter; Danish itself has NO long consonants, so doubled letters are read as a single consonant (they only signal the preceding short vowel). This is encoded with data only: doubled letters are grapheme keys mapping to a length-marked consonant (⟨bb⟩→/bː/), consonant clusters are grapheme keys mapping to the concatenated phonemes (⟨st⟩→/sd/), the vowel-shortening allophone rules fire on `followed_by_phoneme` = those cluster/geminate phonemes, and a second set of rules degeminates /Cː/→/C/. SCHWA: unstressed ⟨e⟩ is [ə], the single most frequent segment in the language. SCHWA + R: an unstressed schwa next to /r/ is not two segments but the single vowel [ɐ] (Puggaard-Rode 2023:39). The schwa raises in both orders, but the /r/ is absorbed into it only where /r/ is itself weak — post-vocalic, the semivowel [ɐ̯] of his Table 2.3 of weak allophones. After a consonant the rhotic is strong and survives. This spec therefore writes hedder [ˈhɛðɐ], sanger [ˈsaŋɐ], store [ˈsdoːɐ] and dyre [ˈdyːɐ] without the rhotic, and klatre [ˈklatʁɐ], andre [ˈanʁɐ] and sikre [ˈsikʁɐ] with it. ⟨y⟩ is declared a vowel letter so that this and every other vowel-conditioned rule reads it correctly; the closed Latin letter set calls ⟨y⟩ a consonant, which also blocked the soft-d rule after it (bryde was [ˈbʁyːdə], now [ˈbʁyːðə]). Schwa next to a NON-rhotic sonorant also assimilates in speech (falde [ˈfall̩]), but that is variable and neither gold this spec is scored against writes a syllabic sonorant at all, so it is deliberately not encoded. HIGH-VOWEL LOWERING: /i y u/ → [e ø o] before a coda [ŋ] or a coda nasal + consonant (Puggaard-Rode 2023:46, rule (7)): ting [teŋ], synge [ˈsøŋə], tung [toŋ], vinder [ˈvenɐ], bunde [ˈbonə]. The rule is checked against the WikiPron gold and holds in 79/81 ⟨i⟩ words, 10/11 ⟨y⟩ words and 33/38 ⟨u⟩ words before a nasal+⟨d⟩ cluster, and in 137/144, 15/22 and 40/40 before other nasal clusters. Its one systematic miss is the ⟨hund⟩ family (hund, hunde, hundrede), where the ⟨d⟩ is silent so there is no coda cluster; the rule engine reads pre-pass slot state and cannot see that the /d/ is about to be deleted. SOFT D: /d/ after a vowel is the approximant [ð] (mad [mað], gade [ɡæːðə]); phonetically it is a very open semivowel, transcribed [ɤ̯] or [ð̞] elsewhere (Puggaard-Rode 2023:39-40). SILENT D: ⟨nd⟩→[n], ⟨ld⟩→[l], ⟨rd⟩→[ʁ]. NO ASPIRATION AFTER /s/: ⟨sp st sk⟩ → [sb sd sɡ]. This is the Danish lexicographic convention for the unaspirated stops; recent phonetic work writes the same sounds [sp st sk] (Puggaard-Rode 2023:39, following Schachtenhaufen 2022), and the espeak-derived gold uses that second convention, which costs this spec about 144 aligned segments on that row without any disagreement about the sound. R: onset ⟨r⟩ is the uvular [ʁ]; coda r-vocalisation ([ɐ̯]) is NOT encoded. V: written [v]. Basbøll (2005) uses [v] and Puggaard-Rode (2023:39) uses [ʋ], noting that both he and Grønnum (1998) treat the sound as frictionless; the literature is split on the symbol, not on the sound, and the two golds split the same way (WikiPron writes ⟨v⟩ in 764 entries and ⟨ʋ⟩ in 9; the espeak-derived gold writes ⟨ʋ⟩), so the symbol is left alone. A-QUALITY: /a/ retracts to [ɑ] next to /r/. H: /h/ is syllable-initial only, so ⟨h⟩ is silent in a coda and in ⟨hv hj⟩ (hvor [voːʁ], hjem [jɛm]). G-ELISION: single intervocalic ⟨g⟩ after a long vowel drops (tage [tæːə]). IG: the ⟨ig⟩ digraph is the adjectivizing suffix and is short [-i] word-finally (Puggaard-Rode 2023:64), and is not a digraph at all when a second ⟨g⟩ follows — ligge, kigge, tigge are ⟨li-gg-e⟩ and now surface as [ˈliɡə] rather than [ˈliːə]. ET: the ⟨-et⟩ suffix is left as [-ət]. It varies stylistically and regionally between [-ɤ] and [-ət] (Puggaard-Rode 2023:58 n.27, citing Petersen et al. 2021); the espeak-derived gold writes the first variant in 81 aligned segments, but both are attested and the spec is not moved onto one gold's choice. STØD is suprasegmental and is not encoded. It cannot be: stødbasis (a bimoraic rhyme — long vowel, diphthong, or short vowel + sonorant; obstruents are never moraic) is necessary but not sufficient, and nothing in the orthography marks it. Both golds write it and both write it differently: WikiPron uses ⟨ˀ⟩, the espeak-derived gold uses ⟨ˤ⟩. WHAT THE espeak-derived ROW MEASURES: it is an AGREEMENT row against espeak-ng's Danish voice, not an accuracy row against Danish, and its stød marking is not usable as evidence. 1302 of its 2233 tokens carry a stød mark (1676 marks in all); 328 tokens carry TWO OR MORE, which Danish does not permit — stød is at most one per stress group; and 224 place it on a short vowel followed by a voiceless stop, a rhyme that has no stødbasis at all. espeak-ng's own output shows why: it emits ⟨ʔ⟩ both for stød and as an epenthetic glottal onset (de [dˈʔi], flere [flˈʔeʔʌ], ikke [ˈʔekə]), and the corpus postprocessor rewrites every one of them as a stød mark. Folding the mark out of both sides moves that row from PER 0.4485 to 0.4146 and exact match from 4.4% to 9.5%; folding ⟨ʁ⟩/⟨r⟩ as well gives 0.3964, and also folding ⟨sb sd sɡ⟩/⟨sp st sk⟩ gives 0.3776. Roughly seven of the remaining PER points on that row are transcription convention. Neither gold writes [ɑ] consistently — WikiPron spells it ⟨a⟩ in the large majority of tokens — so the retraction rules cost PER against notation, not against pronunciation. KNOWN GAP: the short-vowel lowering class beyond the nasal environment (ikke [ˈeɡə], fisk [fesɡ], til [ˈtel]) is lexicalised — bunde [ˈbonə] and hunde [ˈhunə] are a minimal pair with opposite outcomes — so it is not derivable from the spelling and is pinned only as a seed word list (o2i task #80). WIKIPRON ROW: against the wikipron/dan_latn_broad gold (n=4331, PER 0.3455), stod is marked in 20.8% of scored words (901/4331) and, as elsewhere, the orthography gives no basis to place it; folding the mark out of both sides (the engine never emits one) moves PER only to 0.3288 -- stod is not the dominant contributor on this gold, contrary to the a-priori suspicion. The two larger movers are this gold's own symbol choices, not spec defects: it transcribes the onset/coda rhotic with plain <r> where this spec writes the phonetically explicit uvular [ʁ] (Grønnum and Puggaard-Rode use [ʁ]; Basbøll's phonemic /r/ is the same cover symbol wikipron follows), a fold that alone would move PER to 0.2919; and it writes post-s stop clusters voiceless (sk st sp) where this spec writes the lexicographic unaspirated-stop convention (sɡ sd sb) used throughout the rest of this file, moving PER to 0.3232. Both are notation, not accuracy, and are documented rather than folded into a ceiling: folding a gold's own symbol convention into valid_ceiling would credit the spec's own correctness as an input limitation. Folding all three at once (stod + r/ʁ + s-cluster) reaches 0.2509 as a diagnostic upper bound, still short of a defensible ceiling and mixing a legitimate fold with two illegitimate ones, so no valid_ceiling is recorded for this row. The residual g-elision mismatch (wikipron retains a weak fricative/glide reflex of intervocalic ⟨g⟩ in 98/4331 words, e.g. bage [ˈbaːɣə]/[ˈbaːjə], where this spec elides it) is the same documented, variable, unencoded process as the falde/[ˈfall̩] case above, and vowel-only narrow diacritics in this gold total under 100 occurrences across all 4331 words, too rare to be a driver.

sources.notes: Open-access dissertation whose second chapter is a full survey of Danish segmental phonology, and the source actually READ for the rules added here: the consonant tables and their transcription conventions and the table of weak allophones (p.39), schwa-r fusion /rə/ → [ɐ] for the weak (semivowel) allophones (p.39) with the post-consonantal rhotic retained in klatre [ˈkʰlætʁɐ] (p.40) against the imperative klatr! [ˈkʰlætɐ] (p.41), the ⟨-er⟩ order of the same fusion (p.111 n.18, after Basbøll 2005), high-vowel lowering before a coda nasal cluster or [ŋ] (p.46, rule (7)), the [-ɤ ~ -ət] variation in the ⟨-et⟩ suffix (p.58 n.27), stødbasis as a bimoraic rhyme (p.45), and the adjectivizing suffix ⟨-ig⟩ = [-i] (p.64, ex.(19)).

allophone_rules.notes: Unstressed ⟨-er⟩ is one vowel [ɐ], not the two segments [əʁ]: schwa and an adjacent /r/ fuse. Puggaard-Rode (2023:39) states the assimilation as /rə/ → [ɐ] and derives it from the semivowel row of his Table 2.3 of weak allophones, restating Brink & Lund 1975 ch.32, Basbøll 2005 ch.11 and Schachtenhaufen 2010b; the ⟨-er⟩ order is stated at p.111 n.18, where [ɐ] is derived from underlying /-ər/ after Basbøll (2005). His transcriptions in this environment are sanger [ˈsɑ.ŋɐ] (p.47, ex.(9)) and the verbalizing suffix [-ˈeːˀɐ] -ere (p.46). This rule writes the vowel; DA_R_ABSORBED_AFTER_SCHWA removes the /r/ that was fused into it.
The /r/ half of the ⟨-er⟩ fusion — see DA_SCHWA_TO_A_BEFORE_R. Both rules read pre-pass slot state, so they fire on the same ⟨e⟩⟨r⟩ pair regardless of slot order.

The mirror environment, ⟨-re⟩: the unstressed schwa is [ɐ] whether or not the preceding /r/ survives. Puggaard-Rode transcribes the infinitive klatre as [ˈkʰlætʁɐ] (2023:40), with the rhotic intact and the schwa already raised. The post-vocalic case is not one of his examples; this spec writes store [ˈsdoːɐ], where the /r/ is absorbed as well. That absorption is the business of DA_R_ABSORBED_BEFORE_SCHWA, which fires only in weak position.

The /r/ half of the ⟨-re⟩ fusion, restricted to WEAK (post-vocalic) /r/. Puggaard-Rode (2023:39) states the assimilation /rə/ → [ɐ] for the semivowels of Table 2.3, the weak allophones, where /r/ is [ɐ̯]; the approximant [ʁ] is listed there as only marginal in weak position, and he adds (p.40) that weak [ʁ] survives only in a small set of imperatives. A post-consonantal /r/ is therefore not in weak position and is not absorbed: he transcribes the infinitive klatre as [ˈkʰlætʁɐ] (p.40), and the rhotic-less [ˈkʰlætɐ] (p.41) is his transcription of the imperative klatr!, where the schwa is gone. So this spec writes andre [ˈanʁɐ] and sikre [ˈsikʁɐ] with the rhotic, and store [ˈsdoːɐ] and dyre [ˈdyːɐ] without it; none of those four are his transcriptions.

High vowels lower before a coda [ŋ]: /i y u/ → [e ø o] (Puggaard-Rode 2023:46, rule (7)). ting [teŋ], kylling [ˈkyleŋ]. Length is neutralised in this position — only short vowels occur before [ŋ] — so the long target maps to the short surface.
/y/ member of the lowering rule — synge [ˈsøŋə], gynge [ˈɡøŋə]. See DA_LOWER_I_BEFORE_NG.
/u/ member of the lowering rule — tung [toŋ], unge [ˈoŋə]. See DA_LOWER_I_BEFORE_NG. The espeak-derived gold writes [ɒ] here rather than [o]; [o] is the value the description gives.
The second environment of the same lowering rule: /i y u/ → [e ø o] before a coda nasal + consonant (Puggaard-Rode 2023:46, rule (7)). vinder [ˈvenɐ], vinter [ˈventɐ], simpel [ˈsempəl].
/y/ member — pynt [pønt]. See DA_LOWER_I_BEFORE_NASAL_CLUSTER.

/u/ member — bunde [ˈbonə], bump [bomp], gunst [ɡonsd]. See DA_LOWER_I_BEFORE_NASAL_CLUSTER. Over-fires on the ⟨hund⟩ family, where the ⟨d⟩ is silent so there is no coda cluster to trigger the rule: hund, hunde, hundrede keep [u]. The rule engine reads pre-pass slot state, so it cannot see that DA_SILENT_D is about to remove the /d/, and the exception is left standing rather than pinned as a word list.
The adjectivizing suffix ⟨-ig⟩ is short unstressed [-i], not long [-iː]: syndig [ˈsønti] (Puggaard-Rode 2023:64, ex.(19), after Rischel 1970a).

⟨ligge, kigge, tigge⟩ are ⟨li-gg-e⟩, not ⟨lig-g-e⟩: the longest-match tokenizer reads the first two letters as the ⟨ig⟩ digraph and lengthens the vowel, which is wrong wherever a second ⟨g⟩ follows. Restoring the short vowel and its /ɡ/ here gives ligge [ˈliɡə] instead of [ˈliːə]; DA_G_AFTER_IG_DELETE removes the second ⟨g⟩, which spells the same single consonant (Danish has no geminates).
The second ⟨g⟩ of ⟨ligge, kigge, tigge⟩ — see DA_IG_BEFORE_G_NOT_A_DIGRAPH.

/a/ is retracted to [ɑ] adjacent to /r/ (fra [fʁɑ], rar [ʁɑː]); [a] and [ɑ] are in near-complementary distribution conditioned by a neighbouring /r/ (Grønnum 2005; Basbøll 2005).
Long counterpart of DA_A_RETRACT_AFTER_R_SHORT (Grønnum 2005; Basbøll 2005).
/a/ is retracted to [ɑ] before /r/ (har [hɑː], par [pɑː]) — the mirror environment of DA_A_RETRACT_AFTER_R_SHORT (Grønnum 2005; Basbøll 2005).
Long counterpart of DA_A_RETRACT_BEFORE_R_SHORT (Grønnum 2005; Basbøll 2005).

/h/ occurs syllable-initially only (Basbøll 2005), so a coda ⟨h⟩ is silent: øh [øː], åh [ɔː]. The onset ⟨h⟩ of uhyre and uhyggelig is untouched now that ⟨y⟩ is declared a vowel letter and the syllabifier reads ⟨u.hy.re⟩ correctly.

Single intervocalic ⟨g⟩ after a long vowel is elided: tage [tæːə], sige [siːə]. After a short vowel it is retained (bygge [byɡə]), so the rule is restricted to the long-vowel context and to the single-letter grapheme. Claim is standard (e.g. Grønnum 2005); edition not consulted.
⟨dd⟩ is the soft d as well: sidde [siðə]. Same lenition as DA_SOFT_D — doubled ⟨d⟩ only signals the short vowel, it does not block the approximant (Grønnum 2005; Basbøll 2005).

⟨d⟩ is silent after ⟨n l r⟩ (mand, guld, gård); the cluster still shortens the preceding vowel

Danish short stressed high/mid vowels lower in a large, partly-conditioned class that keeps the spelling of the historical higher vowel: against the WikiPron gold, stressed ⟨i⟩→[e] in 111 words, ⟨y⟩→[ø] in 61, ⟨u⟩→[o] in 64, and ⟨ø⟩→[œ] in 68 (near-categorical before ⟨r⟩). til [ˈtel] is one instance (Grønnum 2005; Basbøll 2005). This entry is a SEED LIST pinning a frequent member of the class, not the full generalisation; the conditioned environment for the rest of the class is tracked as follow-up (o2i task #80).

nul [ˈnol] lowers its historical /u/ to [o] while keeping the ⟨u⟩ spelling (Grønnum 2005; Basbøll 2005) — one of 64 stressed ⟨u⟩→[o] words in the WikiPron gold; SEED LIST member, see DA_LEXICAL_LOWER_TIL (o2i task #80 tracks the full class).

kys [ˈkøs] lowers its historical /y/ to [ø] while keeping the ⟨y⟩ spelling (Grønnum 2005; Basbøll 2005) — one of 61 stressed ⟨y⟩→[ø] words in the WikiPron gold; SEED LIST member, see DA_LEXICAL_LOWER_TIL (o2i task #80 tracks the full class).

søn [ˈsœn] lowers its historical /ø/ to [œ] while keeping the ⟨ø⟩ spelling (Grønnum 2005; Basbøll 2005) — one of 68 stressed ⟨ø⟩→[œ] words in the WikiPron gold, near-categorical before ⟨r⟩; SEED LIST member, see DA_LEXICAL_LOWER_TIL (o2i task #80 tracks the full class).

wikipron.measured: Raw PER 0.3455 (n=4331). Stod, the true input-limitation (unwritten in the orthography, marked in 901/4331 gold entries), folds PER to only 0.3288 -- a small movement, not the dominant driver. The larger movers are this gold's own notation choices for the uvular rhotic (r vs [ʁ], folds to 0.2919) and post-s stop voicing (sk/st/sp vs this spec's sɡ/sd/sb convention, folds to 0.3232); these are documented as convention, not folded into valid_ceiling, per the rule against crediting the spec's own correctness as an input limitation. All three combined reach 0.2509, short of a defensible ceiling and mixing legitimate and illegitimate folds, so no valid_ceiling is recorded.
